title: Probing LLMs for hate speech detection: strengths and vulnerabilities
measurement_description: The paper evaluates the capability of Large Language Models to detect hate speech, which includes attacks on individuals or groups based on their religion, as defined in the HateXplain dataset.
findings: The paper uses the Pittsburgh synagogue shooting as a motivating example for the real-world harm of hate speech. The error analysis reveals that models can misclassify hateful posts containing religious slurs (e.g., 'muzrat', a derogatory term for Muslims) as normal, attributing this failure to vocabulary gaps. This indicates a specific vulnerability of the models in detecting religion-based hate speech.
